items.title: AI detectors incorrectly flag essays of non-native English speakers; students should not be penalised: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday said students should not be held guilty of academic misconduct solely on the basis of software that identifies their work as AI-generated. He cited a 2023 study which found that seven widely used AI detectors incorrectly flagged more than three in five essays by non-native English speakers as machine-generated. “ In a Commonwealth where so many students write in English as a second or third language, an honest student could thus be branded a cheat on the strength of a number that no one can explain, and that student cannot meaningfully challenge. No student should therefore be held guilty of misconduct on the word of a machine alone ,” he cautioned. The Chief Justice was delivering the inaugural address at the Commonwealth Legal Education Association’s (CLEA) first Annual International Conference on Legal Education in Hyderabad. CJI Kant further went on to oppose a blanket ban on generative AI in legal education, calling it neither practical nor wise. “ A ban (on AI) would only drive this use out of sight, where it can be neither guided nor examined. items.title: Supreme Court allows bike taxis in Karnataka, rejects State's appeal to restore ban
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the Karnataka government's appeal challenging the Karnataka High Court's decision to allow bike taxi services to operate in the State. A Bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh passed the ruling. Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and Justice NK Singh While pronouncing the verdict today, Justice Sharma also recounted a conversation he had with young women working in his office who used bike taxis. “I asked them, how do you come to my office? They said on a motorbike because they do not have the money to hire a cab. I asked them, why don't you take an auto? They said, ‘Sir, it is five times (the fare) ," Justice Sharma remarked.
